readme.help: Check README.md and README.pt-BR.md against the README standard (read-only)
readme.check.help: Check the README files in a directory (exit 2 when there are findings)
readme.arg.dir: Directory that holds the README files (default: the current directory)
readme.arg.no_twin: Do not compare README.md with README.pt-BR.md
readme.arg.credits_last: Require a Credits heading and check that it is the last second-level heading (default: check it when the heading exists)
readme.finding.readme_missing: README.md was not found in this directory.
readme.finding.twin_missing: README.pt-BR.md was required but was not found.
readme.finding.title_count: Expected exactly one first-level heading, found {count}.
readme.finding.title_first: Text comes before the first-level heading. Only an image or logo block may precede it.
readme.finding.forbidden_section: The section "{heading}" belongs in a dedicated file. Link to the file from another section instead.
readme.finding.link_missing: The relative link target does not exist: {target}
readme.finding.link_outside_root: The link target is absolute or leaves the repository: {target}
readme.finding.admonition_kind: Unknown admonition kind [!{kind}]. Use NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING or CAUTION.
readme.finding.admonition_syntax: Malformed admonition. Start a blockquote with exactly "> [!KIND]" on its own line, followed by the text on the next quoted lines.
readme.finding.fence_unclosed: This fenced code block is never closed.
readme.finding.fence_language: This fenced code block does not declare a language.
readme.finding.readme_long: The file has {lines} lines; more than {limit} is hard to read. Move detail into the docs.
readme.finding.twin_headings: README.md has {english} second-level headings and README.pt-BR.md has {portuguese}.
readme.finding.twin_link: This file must link to {other} within its first {lines} lines.
readme.finding.twin_code: The code blocks differ from those in {other}; they must be identical.
readme.finding.credits_last: The section "{heading}" must be the last second-level section.
readme.finding.logo_unused: A logo exists at {logo} but the header (before the first second-level heading) does not use it.
